reviewType: Source-only shared-account sub-agent review under requesting-code-review; not independent human review or execution acceptance.
scope: Five concrete uncommitted files, including the untracked helper; exact owned #6064 continuation. No source, Git, GitHub, app, simulator or provider mutation; no tests or native commands executed by this reviewer. Only this report was written.
strengths: The helper requires exactly one metadata row whose UUID matches the selected device, admits only Booted or Shutdown, and preserves nonzero discovery/query exits as failures.

The live path preserves the original selected-device query; the offline path explicitly supplies --directory. Both preserve the fixed CovenCave process/marker predicate and 70-minute lookback, with no simulator boot or global-host fallback.
The workflow keeps discovery and reading under the same 15+5+5+5-second owner, keeps the marker after strict and before Release even after strict failure, and retains independent logs and receipts.

Budget accounting remains 95 minutes for all native/marker wrapper bounds plus 9 minutes for other bounded steps and 3 minutes for uploads: 107 minutes inside the unchanged 108-minute job, retaining one minute.

Real-shell/wrapper/helper contract source preserves live query failure 17 and invalid-destination rejection, and adds shutdown success/failure plus malformed, missing, duplicate, transitional and escaped-store cases. The retained RED log has 8 passes/1 failure; retained GREEN-final has 9 passes/0 failures. These are inspected prior receipts, not a fresh reviewer execution.
Tracked apps/ios bytes match the base and there are no untracked apps/ios files. The original bounce UI-test SHA256 matches bf2c8ca1e8968cad2e4e11651aa9c881371f97365ffdf3baff0a704d62556211.

The design accurately limits the normal-signature local iOS27.2 probe to positive channel evidence and preserves the original shutdown149 and Debug first failure; instrumented strict success does not become uninstrumented/native/frame/device/human acceptance.

findings.title: Reject redirected data and diagnostics directories before choosing the offline store
findings.issue: resolve(strict=True) discards evidence of redirection. The data check then tests only the final UUID/data suffix, and the store check tests only confinement within data. A diagnostics symlink to another directory inside the same data directory is therefore accepted; a data symlink whose target also ends in the selected UUID/data is accepted too. The command then reads the redirected target instead of proving that it is the selected device data/var/db/diagnostics store.
findings.concreteTrigger: For valid Shutdown metadata and an existing selected data directory, let data/var/db/diagnostics be a symlink to data/Library/stale-diagnostics. Lines 43-45 admit the resolved directory because it is a directory beneath data, and line 46 passes that different store to log show. No existing scenario rejects this: escaped-store only points outside data.
findings.impact: A successful query of a substituted or stale store can produce an empty or misleading marker result and contradicts the explicit requirement that redirected directories/stores fail before reading. The design line 19 and plan line 57 currently promise a stronger admission rule than this helper implements.
findings.recommendedRepair: Reject redirection of the selected UUID/data directory and the var/db/diagnostics path components after normalizing any legitimate system-prefix alias such as /var to /private/var. Require the admitted store to remain the actual diagnostics path, rather than any resolved descendant of data. Add real-shell/helper fixtures for an internal diagnostics symlink and a redirected data directory whose target retains the same UUID/data suffix; both must fail before any log invocation.
findings.evidenceClass: Direct source reasoning; no reproduction executed by reviewer.

declinedToJudge: Hosted iOS26.5 behavior and actual app writer-error absence require the future exact-revision collector run; a local iOS27.2 channel probe cannot settle them.
Original uninstrumented e946 strict/local Release failures, frame cost, physical-device behavior and human acceptance remain outside this source-only collector review and are not cleared.

No additional process-ownership finding is asserted from the new Python intermediary: the inspected subprocess.run KeyboardInterrupt path kills its direct child. Adversarial descendant execution was not performed in this source-only review.

assessment.reasoning: The collector boundary and evidence limits are otherwise aligned with the requested correction. Repair R1 and extend the focused contracts before publication; this verdict grants no merge, release or acceptance authority.
